text: Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle touched down on the Moon at Tranquility Base on July 20, 1969 at 20:17 UTC.
Neil Armstrong took semi-manual control during final descent to fly past a crater surrounded by large boulders.
The astronauts spent 21 hours and 36 minutes on the lunar surface, conducting a 2.5-hour moonwalk.
The descent stage ladder bears a plaque inscribed: 'Here men from the planet Earth first set foot upon the Moon July 1969, A.D. We came in peace for all mankind.'
Eagle's ascent stage lifted off from the Moon on July 21, 1969, using the descent stage as a launch pad.
Eagle's descent stage remains at Tranquility Base on the Moon.
Ascent-stage fate differs between sources after being jettisoned in lunar orbit.
safe_text: The ascent stage was jettisoned after crew transfer; historical sources differ on where it eventually impacted the lunar surface.
